claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases under conventional cooling.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 undergoes a complex, multistep crystallization sequence.
Primary crystallization is substantial during the proposed slower-cooling stage.
An additional rapid quench should be applied immediately after the slower-cooling stage and before reheating.
The secondary rapid quench drives the alloy quickly into the supercooled-liquid range.
The secondary quench should be performed just below the onset of primary crystallization and before significant crystal nucleation.
A sufficiently high secondary-quench cooling rate minimizes atomic mobility.
Minimizing atomic mobility inhibits crystalline nucleation and growth.
Suppression of crystalline nucleation and growth produces a finer microstructure.
Suppression of crystalline nucleation and growth increases retained amorphous content.
Reducing the time available for atomic rearrangement freezes in a disordered amorphous state.
The secondary rapid quench raises the crystallization-onset temperature during subsequent reheating.
A raised crystallization-onset temperature represents enhanced thermal stability.
Relative to the baseline cycle, secondary-quenched samples will have a higher amorphous-phase fraction.
Relative to the baseline cycle, secondary-quenched samples will exhibit a higher DSC crystallization-onset temperature.
The standard rapid-cooling, slower-cooling, and reheating cycle produces extensive primary crystallization.
The standard thermal cycle yields low amorphous retention and limited thermal stability.
The beneficial effect requires a sufficiently high secondary-quench cooling rate.
Below the required secondary-quench rate, primary crystallization will not be adequately suppressed.

contradictions.description: The intervention is placed after a slower-cooling stage in which primary crystallization is said to be substantial, but it is also required to occur before significant crystal nucleation. A quench after substantial crystallization cannot kinetically prevent the nuclei and crystals that have already formed.

The intervention says cooling rapidly after the slower-cooling stage forces the alloy into the supercooled-liquid range, while the conditions say the quench begins within that range just below crystallization onset. The starting thermal state and direction through the stated window are therefore ambiguous.
